How Election Controversies Can Now Become History
While I fully support this, I think it's a bit optimistic to think it would end claims of hacking.

I don't know if it would end claims of hacking, but I think the article is correct in saying it would make hacking much more difficult if all ballot images were posted as public record. It is incredibly difficult to alter a digital image and then alter the paper record linked to it in exactly the same way, down to the pixel, without tell-tale artifacts that image experts can spot. Also this would be prohibitively time consuming. Claims of hacking would have to get around these hard facts to be credible. This is a great system if we use it.
That type of fix doesn't address the claims of fraud by immigrant voters, deceased voters, etc.

This is very true. However, machine-hacking is by far the most problematic type of fraud. Voter fraud requires someone to submit a fraudulent physical ballot, fraudulent either because they are not qualified to vote, or by mail for entirely fictitious voters. This latter is a good argument to reverse the trend in many states to voting by mail, which has a much weaker chain of custody. No one knows what is being done with all those votes while they are sitting in an election department for days. Vote by mail should be for good excuse, such as disabled, deployed, work trip, etc. Voting is a right and a privilege which merits some inconvenience for a best-practices system.

Voter fraud is far more risky to perpetrate than machine hacking for the simple reason that machine hacking leaves no fingerprints. A voter who requests a voting list and then challenges a voter's status may be entitled an answer, as various state and local laws require. Why risk all that when you can tunnel into a VPN, insert malware, and give your guys as many votes as you want with a couple of keystrokes? And with the laws as they stand, no one will ever find out, because there is no verification of final vote counts of the type that the digital ballot images allow.

Yes, people will always find some way to complain they've been cheated, but that is no reason to not move to a modern, transparent, best practices system in elections. The point is not to entirely eliminate accusations of cheating. The point is to make cheating much, much more difficult. Right now it is way, way too easy.
